Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
54-year-old male with untreated hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, and smoking history presenting with 2-hour mid-sternal pressure-type chest discomfort radiating to left arm, associated dyspnoea, light-headedness and nausea—high clinical suspicion for acute coronary syndrome; ambulance arranged for ED evaluation.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden-onset chest “pressure” (7/10) began while gardening; constant for ~2 h, unchanged at rest.  
• Radiation: Left shoulder/arm.  
• Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath, light-headedness, persistent nausea (no vomiting), recent progressive exertional dyspnoea, calf pain and leg swelling on exertion.  
• Pertinent negatives: No dysphagia, no vomiting, no bowel/bladder change, no head radiation of pain.  
• Past medical history: Hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia (both untreated).  
• Medications: None.  
• Allergies: Not documented.  
• Social: Current smoker (quantity not stated); lives with wife; limited physical activity except fortnightly gardening.  
• Preventive health: Not discussed.

Examination:
• Remote video—no vitals or physical findings available.  
• No diaphoresis or syncope reported during call.

Impression:
1. Acute Coronary Syndrome (unstable angina/NSTEMI) – most likely given classic pressure-type chest pain with left-arm radiation, autonomic symptoms, onset with mild exertion, and multiple cardiac risk factors (HTN, hyperlipidaemia, smoking, male >50 y).  
2. Pulmonary Embolism – consider due to acute dyspnoea plus calf pain/leg swelling, but chest pain quality and risk profile favour ACS.  
3. Aortic Dissection – lower likelihood; pain described as pressure without back radiation.

Plan:
• Emergency management: 999 ambulance arranged; patient advised to remain calm, sit upright, sip water, avoid taking any medications until assessed.  
• Handover: Clinician to relay history to paramedics; hospital team to be notified for immediate assessment.  
• Expected ED work-up: ECG, serial cardiac enzymes, chest X-ray, basic labs, possible CT angiography if PE or dissection suspected (per DDx context).  
• Follow-up: Clinician will review hospital findings and schedule post-hospital appointment.  
• Education/Reassurance: Explained need to rule out heart and lung causes; outlined ambulance and ED procedures.

Quality checks:

● Missing elements: Drug allergies, exact smoking quantity, family cardiac history, vitals/exam findings, current weight/BMI, complete medication list (OTC/supplements), follow-up timeframe specifics.  
● Transcript vs DDx conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear but lacked allergy response and objective examination/vitals; otherwise coherent.
